A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STACI for topology-aware conformal prediction on stream networks. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original tail-up simulations and PeMS traffic experiments, including coverage, prediction-set efficiency, hyperparameter analyses, and an offline ablation.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation and traffic results, expanded road/backbone comparisons, perturbation experiments, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Mahalanobis score, covariance mixture, tail-up estimator, and ACI update remain unchanged. However, Algorithm 1, line 9 changes a quantile instruction into a normalized-rank 'largest element' instruction, which is inconsistent with the retained quantile definition. This changes the written inference specification without establishing an actual implementation change.

E1.justification: The synthetic processes and original 12-sensor traffic network remain; the latter is identifiable as PeMS-G1 from the matching maps. v2 adds a second 12-sensor road network, PeMS-G2, and imperfect-topology evaluation conditions. These extend coverage beyond the original clean-network scenarios; the more specific PeMS03 name alone is not a new dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds MultiDimSPCI (local) to the traffic comparisons. Appendix D.5 and Table 3 additionally evaluate CopulaCPTS, inconsistently called CopulaTSCP in prose, and DeepSTUQ against STACI. These introduce substantive comparator families beyond v1's geometric conformal baselines.

E3.justification: Reported defaults change from n=300 to 500, lambda=0.5 to 0.6, and 3,000 to 5,000 real-data test observations; v1 already used n=500 for Figure 5. v2 adds ASTGCN and STGODE evaluation configurations, perturbation protocols, and runtime comparisons. These are reported setting changes, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds imperfect-topology robustness tests, temporal-shift summaries, runtime/scaling analysis, and hyperparameter sweeps across six road/backbone combinations. The robustness protocol is inconsistent: Appendix D.6 describes added edges, whereas Table 4 describes Gaussian coordinate noise. The offline covariance ablation is retained from v1 Appendix C.2, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 2 explicitly reports ten seeds, and Figure 3 identifies standard-deviation bands. v2 removes these disclosures while retaining the plotted uncertainty and reporting mean±standard deviation in tables. The PDFs do not establish a change in actual run counts or a new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds results across road/backbone combinations and new baseline, perturbation, distribution-shift, and runtime results. Table 3 reports STACI coverage/inefficiency of 95.75%/67.54 versus DeepSTUQ's 93.82%/66.51, demonstrating a coverage-volume tradeoff rather than superiority on both metrics. Changed experimental settings prevent interpreting the expanded results as same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1 Theorem 5.5 becomes v2 Theorem 2 with the new restriction alpha<alpha_0. Appendix A.2 replaces the pairwise-majorization argument with a Dirichlet–Jensen tail lemma and revised proof. Separately, the moved ACI proposition changes limiting miscoverage from alpha to 1-alpha, introducing an inconsistency with the unchanged ACI update.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same topology-aware conformal framework, validity, efficiency, and empirical-superiority claims. The conclusion now explicitly excludes full-graph joint prediction sets over hundreds of nodes and proposes composing smaller subgraph sets, narrowing the stated practical scope.

C2.justification: The new limitations section restricts the intended application to roughly 2–30-dimensional subgraphs and explains dimensionality-related problems. Appendix D adds interpretations of copula instability, DeepSTUQ's missing joint-coverage guarantee, computational costs, and topology robustness. The earlier limitation concerning adaptive finite-sample coverage remains in Appendix C rather than being newly added.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware specifications, PeMS03 dates and sensor counts, dataset provenance, backbone implementation sources and licenses, and training/runtime information in Appendix D. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's simulation-generation details and project link. The STACI project link itself remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 more explicitly distinguishes static-graph conformal tasks from spatiotemporal forecasting. Appendix B adds PID and Bellman conformal approaches, while new references support backbones and dimensionality discussions; the old majorization reference disappears with its proof argument. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: Algorithm 1 and the adaptive-coverage analysis move into the appendices, mathematical exposition is condensed, a limitations section and contents page appear, and the experimental appendix receives a much more detailed structure. Related-work and experimental discussion are also rewritten, although the abstract and much introductory prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 merges the two simulation figures, replaces the traffic comparison scatterplot with an expanded table, adds four supplementary tables, expands and relocates the road-network illustration, and adds a large hyperparameter figure grid. It also adopts a substantially different document layout. The offline plots are retained and relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The broader road/backbone comparisons and implementation disclosures improve support and reproducibility beyond v1's single-road, single-backbone evaluation. The qualified efficiency theorem and explicit dimensionality limitations also improve precision. These benefits are tempered by the newly inconsistent ACI proposition, malformed quantile instruction, conflicting robustness descriptions, and lost seed disclosure, limiting the net quality gain.
